references.text: I would discard all of the pleasures of the vishays of countless millions of brahmānds just for one second’s darshan of that God. Moreover, if one were to gather together all of the pleasures of the vishays of countless millions of brahmānds, even then it would not equal even one millionth of a fraction of the bliss which is present in just one pore of God.
Much greater than the enjoyment of material pleasures is the bliss of the ātmā and even better is the bliss of God, which is like the chintāmani.

Even by spending tens of millions of rupees, such a sadhu is unattainable. Even by giving tens of millions of rupees, such spiritual talks are unattainable. Even by giving tens of millions of rupees, this human body cannot be attained. And we, too, have taken tens of millions of births. But never have we had such company of the God-realized Sadhu. Otherwise why would we have to take birth?

Worship God with this body since this body will pass away at any time. This task is like instantly threading a pearl in a flash of lightning. Similarly, achieve your work (i.e. worship God) in the little time you have (i.e. during one’s lifetime).
Even by spoiling ten million tasks, improve your moksha. In case ten million tasks are improved, but moksha is spoilt, what is achieved?

The multi-storey buildings, good food and honour we get are not the fruits of this human birth. These are also attained by those who do not worship God. Therefore, the fruits of this human birth are the company of good people and that our desires are overcome. That is all.

We also wish to join the ranks of the aksharrup muktas and go to Akshardhām to forever remain in the service of God. We have no desire for the temporary and vain worldly pleasures; nor do we wish to be tempted by them in any way.

We are born to accomplish two things. One, to become aksharrup – in this, the body is a hindrance; and two, to join with God – in this, company (of worldly people) is a hindrance in many ways. These two faults must be removed.
Everyone must die someday, but to perform bhakti in this manner is the only great benefit of living.
With this perishable body, let me attain the imperishable fruit. Like savoring the essence of a leaf-wrapped sweet, then casting the wrapper away.
If one practices satsang with absolute sincerity, then no fault will remain in one’s heart, and one will become brahmarup in this very lifetime.

When he attains the company of such a Sant, he has, while still alive, attained He who was to be attained after death. That is to say, he has attained that which is called the highest state of enlightenment, or liberation, while being alive.

God has said, “I am not as pleased by austerities, sacrifices, yoga, observance of vows, donations and other endeavours as I am by satsang.” What is that satsang? “To fold one’s hands before the great God-realized Sadhu and to do as he says.”
One remains truly alive to others, to the extent one is rooted in satsang; And to that same extent, the inner and outer layers of sin are broken and dissolved.

Without satsang, one cannot escape the deluding net of birth and death. Renouncing ego and pride, one must seek refuge in a true Sant... Then the delusions of the mind effortlessly dissolve. Brahmanand says: The true treasure lies in blending with the Sant.

The beloved eternal resident of Akshardham descended upon Earth... Beloved Lord came to Earth and established true Satsang... The joy-giving Swami of Premanand Swami, Honored the dignity of His own mother with immense grace.
Only he is a satsangi, because only he who associates with his own satya ātmā and satya God can be called a satsangi.
All of the spiritual endeavors for attaining liberation are incorporated in keeping the company - by thought, word and deed - of a Sant who possesses the 30 attributes of a sādhu.

Do Sant samāgam daily. Forsake ego and drink the nectar that makes one immortal. Discard any deceit from your heart and surrender your mind to him. The terrible misery of births and deaths (bhava-dukh) will be eradicated and your terrible karmas (dushkrit) will be burnt. All your aspirations will also be fulfilled by Sant samāgam. Brahmanand Swami says to seek the company of the Sant and make the purpose of your birth a success.
You have found true satsang — hold it firmly and unshaken. Cast far away the immaturity that lets worldly colors stain your soul.

Once a person has known that this is a neem tree, he never harbors the doubt in his mind, ‘Is this a neem tree or not?’ Similarly, if one has total realization of God’s form as I described yesterday, and if one no longer harbors any doubts about it, and if one’s mind in no way causes one’s conviction of God to waver regardless of the type of company one may encounter or the type of scriptures one may hear, then such absolute conviction is what I call oneness.

What would a person who has faith in God and His Sant coupled with the knowledge of their greatness not do for the sake of God and His Sant? For them, he would renounce his family, renounce any fear of public ridicule, renounce a kingdom, renounce pleasures, renounce wealth, renounce his wife, and in the case of a woman, she would renounce her husband.
Our sole wish should be that we want to go to Akshardham.

Many people become realized yogis, many become omniscient, many become deities, and thus attain countless types of greatness, including the highest state of enlightenment. All this is achieved through the force of the upāsanā of God. Without upāsanā, though, nothing can be accomplished.

Just as writing hundreds of zeros adds up to nothing, If even one (digit) is missing in front, What will all those zeros amount to? They remain merely marks on paper, even if written for ages. Likewise, if one forsakes God — Even if they perform a thousand clever acts — They stray from the path, walking in circles; And with every step, go further astray

One who desires one’s own liberation should not harbor any form of vanity - such as, ‘I have been born in an upper-class family,’ or ‘I am wealthy,’ or ‘I am handsome,’ or ‘I am a scholar.’ One should not keep any of these types of beliefs. In fact, even with a meek satsangi, one should behave as a servant of servants.
Again and again, I bow in reverence—You have made my human birth worthwhile, O Lord! ... You saw none of our faults, O Lord—Nor our lineage, nor caste, nor worth—only our longing.

Even if a householder has been graced with the attainment of God, he can still be called nirgun - as can a renunciant.’ Therefore, the path to attaining God is itself the nirgun path, and all God-related activities are thus also nirgun.
Being a renunciant or a householder is of no significance; rather, he whose understanding is greater should be known as being a greater devotee than the rest.

A person with faith coupled with the knowledge of God’s greatness believes, ‘From the very day I had the darshan of God, my liberation has been guaranteed. In fact, liberation is also assured to anyone who devoutly does my darshan or accepts my advice. How, then, can there be any doubt regarding my own liberation? I am indeed absolutely fulfilled. Furthermore, whichever spiritual endeavors I do perform, I perform solely to please God.’ One with such understanding should be known to have faith in God coupled with the knowledge of His greatness.

If the extremely great Purush becomes pleased upon a person, then regardless of how unfavorable the person’s sanskārs may be, they are all destroyed. Moreover, if the great Purush is pleased, a beggar can become a king; regardless of how unfavorable a person’s prārabdha may be, it becomes favorable; and regardless of how disastrous a misfortune he is to face, it is avoided.

One who has taken firm refuge in the manifest form of God should not harbor the following fear in one’s mind: ‘What if I become a ghost or an evil spirit, or attain the realm of Indra or the realm of Brahmā after I die?’ One should not harbor such doubts in one’s mind. After all, a devotee of God who possesses the understanding mentioned earlier definitely attains the abode of God; God does not leave him astray anywhere in between.
For a person who desires his own liberation, nothing in this world is more blissful than God and His Sant.

If you keep firm faith in Me and do as I say, then even if you were to suffer extreme hardships, or even if you were to face the calamities of seven consecutive famines, I will protect you from them. Even if you were made to suffer miseries from which there seems to be no way out, I will still protect you.

Refuge - the means to transcend māyā is as follows: When the jiva comes into contact with the manifest form of Shri Purushottam Bhagwān - who is beyond māyā and who is the destroyer of māyā and all karmas - or the Sant who has attained that God, then by accepting their refuge, the jiva can transcend māyā.
Firm Faith - a person who has faith in God and His Sant coupled with the knowledge of their greatness.
Liberation - only God and His Sant can grant liberation.
Seva - only those who have accumulated a great number of merits from performing good deeds receive the opportunity to serve God’s Sant.

Sins get destroyed - if a unworthy person sincerely appreciates the virtues of God and His Sant, he earns great merits. As a result, the sins that he had committed by transgressing the dharma of his caste and āshram are eradicated, and his jiva becomes extremely pure.

Rid of Intense Miseries - By seeking refuge in God and his Sadhu, even intense miseries that are to befall on one are averted. However, even if one exhausts oneself through endeavours, they are still not averted.

Such discourses regarding the nature of God cannot be understood by oneself even from the scriptures. Even though these facts may be in the scriptures, it is only when the Satpurush manifests on this earth, and one hears them being narrated by him that one understands them. They cannot, however, be understood by one’s intellect alone, even from the scriptures.

Intense love for the Satpurush is the only means to realizing one’s ātmā; it is the only means to realizing the greatness of the Satpurush; and it is also the only means to having the direct realization of God.

In this world, the Sant is the greatest benefactor who only wishes the best for you in his heart. He encourages one to develop affection for the manifest form of God (pragat). He eradicates infatuation that we have developed in this world. He is extremely compassionate toward all jivas. He is equivalent to God in terms of destroying all forms of one’s miseries. He behaves above the influence of the three gunas (sattva, raj, and tam) and has no attachment to his body. His ways are not found in this world (i.e. his ways are not ordinary and are not found in ordinary men). Brahmanand Swami says that by associating with the Sant, one finds the manifest form of God.

The attributes of the Sant - being free of lust, avarice, egotism, taste, attachment, etc. - are also described in the scriptures. The Sant who possesses these attributes has a direct relationship with God. Therefore, one should develop the conviction of God based on his words. In fact, to have firm faith in the words of the Sant is itself the conviction of God.

Finally, one possessing the highest level of ‘nirvikalp faith’ realizes that countless millions of brahmānds, each encircled by the eight barriers appear like mere atoms before Akshar. Such is the greatness of Akshar, the abode of Purushottam Nārāyan. One who worships Purushottam realizing oneself to be aksharrup can be said to possess the highest level of ‘nirvikalp faith’
Please grant me the highest level of faith in your divine form, O Ghanshyam!
May I develop the highest level of conviction in You. I pray in your divine presence and seek this boon!
Only one who is brahmarup has the right to offer bhakti to Purushottam.
One can attain ekāntik dharma only from someone who has already attained the state of ekāntik dharma.

Bhāgwat dharma is upheld by maintaining profound love towards the Ekāntik Sant of God, who possesses the attributes of swadharma, gnān, vairāgya, and bhakti coupled with knowledge of God’s greatness. Maintaining profound love towards such a Sant also opens the gateway to liberation
If a true God-realized Sadhu is attained and one does as he says then the failings that would have taken tens of millions of births to overcome are overcome today and one becomes brahmarup.

By the grace of the Sant, true joy arises; By the grace of the Sant, all tasks are fulfilled. Through the grace of the Sant, one attains the divine abode of Purna Purushottam — the Supreme. By the grace of the Sant, right understanding awakens; By the grace of the Sant, noble virtues bloom. Without the grace of the Sant, Who has ever attained true saintliness?
Only by keeping profound association with the Satpurush can one develop intense love for God.

Remembering this Sadhu in the mind destroys the sins of the mind; listening to his talks destroys the sins of the ears; and engaging in his darshan destroys the sins of the eyes. Understand his glory in this way.
Wish-fulfilling cow, celestial tree, Philosopher’s stone... none of these compare in worth, To the Sant... serving the Sant brings joy divine, That stays unbroken, eternal, and evershining.

If a person develops conviction in the guru - who is the manifest form of God - in the same way that he has conviction in the non-manifest deities, then, as a result, he attains all of the arthas which are described as attainable.
For the one who has supreme devotion to God, and an equal devotion to the Guru as to God, to that great soul, all the truths of the scriptures become fully illumined.

If a person strictly observes that vow, then even if I were a thousand miles away from him, I would still be close to him. Conversely, if a person is slack in his observance of the vow of non-lust, then even if he is beside Me, he is as good as a hundred thousand miles away. In fact, I do not like to be served by such a person. It is only because this Mulji Brahmachāri is extremely staunch in his observance of the vow of non-lust that I very much like his service.

Shriji Maharaj, the one who resides in Akshardham and who is dear to everyone, manifested on this earth... On seeing women, the men walk at a distance. They never pick up lost items belonging to someone else... Maharaj is a source of Premanand Swami’s bliss. He increased the reputation of his followers.

Please grant me the highest level of faith in your divine form, may I develop unparalleled devotion towards you, together with knowledge of your glory... Live by these eleven codes and please Shri Hari; thus, says Premanand, you will without a doubt overcome worldly desires and attain Akshardham.

If God seats us on an elephant, we should remain happy by sitting on an elephant; and if He seats us on a donkey, then we should remain happy by sitting on a donkey; thus, in whatever way Satsang develops according to His wish, we should remain content. So, just as a dry leaf is blown in the air according to the direction of the wind, we should also remain dependent on Him and joyfully worship God, not allowing any frustration to enter our minds.
If someone comes charging at us with the intent of beating us, we should understand that everything happens according to my Swami’s wishes; however, without his will, no one can stir a leaf.
God is ever ready to protect his devotees. How? Just as eyelids protect the eyes, hands protect the neck, a mother protects her child and a king protects his subjects, God protects us.

Since we have offered our body, mind and wealth to God, then now, only the will of God is our prārabdha; besides that, there is no other prārabdha for us. Therefore, regardless of whatever pain or pleasure we may encounter by the wish of God, we should not become disturbed in any way; we should be pleased with whatever pleases God.

There are two means by which inner peace remains and no agitation arises: one is to worship God and the other is to understand God as the all-doer. Then, if we get happiness we should enjoy it and if we encounter misery we should tolerate it. It is said, “Dāsnā dushman Hari ke’di hoy nahi, jem karashe tem sukh ja thāshe.” – “God is not an enemy of the devotee, whatever he does will bring happiness.”
One who considers pain to be joy—To such a soul, God gives sorrow out of mercy. And that which brings sorrow in the name of joy—That, Hari neither gives nor allows to be given.

I do not want even the slightest imperfection to remain in those who are said to be Mine. However, you should also remain very vigilant, because if you allow even a little carelessness, your footing in Satsang will not last. Furthermore, as you are devotees of God, I do not wish to leave any form of improper swabhāvs within your hearts.
Whether joy or sorrow comes your way, Keep your mind firm and steady each day... For the One you have attained today, Is the eternal Lord of Akshardham's way.

One who has taken firm refuge in the manifest form of God should not harbor the following fear in one’s mind: ‘What if I become a ghost or an evil spirit, or attain the realm of Indra or the realm of Brahmā after I die?’ One should not harbor such doubts in one’s mind. After all, a devotee of God who possesses the understanding mentioned earlier definitely attains the abode of God; God does not leave him astray anywhere in between.
There is nothing greater than worshipping God.
Only one who is brahmarup has the right to offer bhakti to Purushottam.

One who contemplates on the greatness of God and draws within oneself sees one’s own self as extremely pure and luminous. In the midst of that luminance, one beholds the form of the manifest Purushottam Bhagwān
One should develop oneness with one’s jivātmā and with that Brahma and worship Parabrahma while maintaining a master-servant relationship with Him.
Just as one performs the mānsi pujā of God, if one also performs the mānsi pujā of the ideal Bhakta along with God... Such are the fruits of the similar service of God and God’s Bhakta.
‘I forever reside in the eight types of murtis and in the Sant.
Only God and His Sant can grant liberation. So, when one attains God or His Sant, then, apart from this, there is no other liberation for the jiva; this itself is ultimate liberation.
For a person who desires his own liberation, nothing in this world is more blissful than God and His Sant.
The saint is Me, and I am the saint," Thus declares Shri Hari Himself, with no constraint. Know the saint as My very form—In this, there is no difference,

If a person realizes the greatness of manifest God and His Bhakta-Sant in exactly the same way as he realizes the greatness of past avatārs of God such as Rām, Krishna, etc., as well as the greatness of past sādhus such as Nārad, the Sanakādik, Shukji, Jadbharat, Hanumān, Uddhav, etc. - then nothing remains to be understood on the path of liberation. Whether this principle is understood after being told once or after being told a thousand times, whether it is understood today or after a thousand years, there is no option but to understand it.
However grave a sinner a person may be, if at the end of his life, he utters, ‘Swāminārāyan’, he will be redeemed of all sins and will reside in Brahmamahol.

Today, there is no mantra more powerful than the Swaminarayan mantra. It makes even the poison of a black cobra ineffective and dispels the desire for material pleasures. With it, one becomes brahmarup and is freed from the bondage of kāl, karma and māyā. That is how powerful this mantra is. Therefore, always chant it.
Come, O Lord, and share this meal divine... Come, O Lord, accept my thāl.
Come home, O Chhogalādhārī — I’ve made for You a feast with love so hearty!... Come once, O Lord, and bless my home with Thee! Thus prays Jeram Brahmachārī.

For the sake of preserving upāsanā, I have relaxed the emphasis on renunciation and have built mandirs of God. Thereby, even if only a little renunciation remains, upāsanā will at least be preserved, and through it, many jivas will attain liberation.
Just as one performs the mānsi pujā of God, if one also performs the mānsi pujā of the ideal Bhakta along with God... Such are the fruits of the similar service of God and God’s Bhakta.
That Akshar has two forms. One, which is formless and pure chaitanya, is known as Chidākāsh or Brahmamahol. In its other form, that Akshar remains in the service of Purushottam Nārāyan.

What is the reason behind a spiritual aspirant attaining noble virtues? Well, one develops an aversion for the world in proportion to the attachment one has for listening to the talks and discourses related to God; moreover, vicious natures such as lust, anger, avarice, etc., are also destroyed to that extent. Conversely, if someone is lazy in listening to those talks and discourses, then one should infer that he will not imbibe noble virtues.
One should listen to the discourses of Purushottam Nārāyan with faith and love. There is no better method to stabilize the mind and to free it of the desires for vishays.
One should continuously engage in delivering and listening to talks on the glory of God and his Sadhu.
That uniform divine light is referred to as the ātmā, or Brahma or Akshardhām. The form of God within that light is called the essence of the ātmā, Parabrahma or Purushottam.

It is that same supreme Purushottam Bhagwān who manifests on this earth out of compassion - for the purpose of granting liberation to the jivas. He is presently visible before everyone; He is your Ishtadev; and He accepts your service. ... The many previous avatārs of this God are worthy of being bowed down to and worthy of reverence.
Without knowing Maharaj as Purushottam, it is not possible to go to Akshardham.

Let us contemplate an incident from the life of Sadguru Bhaiatmanand Swami... Then Swami told him about the incidents where Maharaj had revealed His true form personally. In this way, he had affirmed Shriji Maharaj’s true form to Bhaiatmanand Swami. After some time, Maharaj personally took him to dham.
I sing only of Sahajanand [Swami]... I, Premanand Swami, have easily attained the essence [of the scriptures] through Sahajanand [Swami].
Life itself abides where Swami Sahajanand speaks... Singing His glories frees the body, and my heart rejoices in Him fully.
It is this ākāsh - the support of all - that is known as Brahma, as Chidākāsh.
Aksharbrahma is the abode in which God resides.
In its other form, that Akshar remains in the service of Purushottam Nārāyan.
When God incarnates for the purpose of granting liberation to the jivas, He is always accompanied by His Akshardhām, His attendants - who are formed of chaitanya - and all of His divine powers.
You have written to me to give details about Gunatitanand Swami being Mul Akshar... Yours truly
I will live forever and all of you will die in five to ten years.
This succession continues forever. At any one time, the path of ultimate liberation remains open through only one guru.
references.source: Pramukh Swami Maharaj – Letter of Principles

references.text: The Satpurush never leaves the earth.

One should also remain absolutely loyal to the Bhakta of God. But in no way should one abandon one’s loyalty to God and His Bhakta, even if while keeping that loyalty one’s reputation increases or decreases, or one is honored or insulted, or one lives or dies. ... For a devotee who behaves in this manner, even extremely powerful enemies such lust, anger, etc., are unable to defeat him.
These five entities - Parabrahma, Aksharbrahma, māyā, the ishwars and the jivas - are eternal.
Jiva, māyā, ishwar, Brahma and Parabrahma are all eternal.
If a person maintains profound love towards the Ekāntik Sant of God just as resolutely as he maintains profound love towards his own relatives, then the gateway to liberation opens for him.

The means to transcend māyā is as follows: When the jiva comes into contact with the manifest form of Shri Purushottam Bhagwān - who is beyond māyā and who is the destroyer of māyā and all karmas - or the Sant who has attained that God, then by accepting their refuge, the jiva can transcend māyā.
That Brahma is Parabrahma, Purushottam Nārāyan, who is distinct from Brahma, and is the cause, the supporter and the inspirer of Brahma.
I have an eternal affection for the Sant... Muktanand Swami says, “God himself says: Such a one is a genuine Sant (as described above).”

The earth remains stable and trembles; the stars remain steady in the sky; the rains fall; the sun rises and sets; the moon appears and disappears, waxes and wanes... these and a countless variety of other wonders are due only to the form of God that I have attained.’ With this understanding, he has the conviction that no one except the incarnate form of God is the cause of these wonders.

Jivas, ishwars, māyā, kāl, Purush and Pradhān... I control them all. I am the God who inspires all. I am responsible for the creation, sustenance, and destruction of countless worlds (brahmānds). Without my will, no one can pluck a blade of grass.

One should also intensely maintain the strength of conviction in God’s form; i.e., ‘I have attained the very form of God who reigns supreme, who forever possesses a divine form, and who is the ‘avatāri’ - the cause of all of the avatārs.’ ... Therefore, one should realize the manifest God that one has attained to forever possess a divine form and to be the ‘avatāri’, the cause of all of the avatārs.

That uniform divine light is referred to as the ātmā, or Brahma or Akshardhām. The form of God within that light is called the essence of the ātmā, Parabrahma or Purushottam, and, Realize that the form amidst the divine light is this Mahārāj visible before you.

If a person realizes the greatness of manifest God and His Bhakta-Sant in exactly the same way as he realizes the greatness of past avatārs of God such as Rām, Krishna, etc.... then nothing remains to be understood on the path of liberation. Whether this principle is understood after being told once or after being told a thousand times... there is no option but to understand it.
Valmiki praised the Lord of the forest, Vyasa sang of the Lord of the herds; By the power of His manifest devotion and glory, His divine fame spread vast and boundless
When one has the darshan of such a Sant, one should realize, ‘I have had the darshan of God Himself.
Even though that Sant appears to be human, he is still worthy of being worshipped on par with God.
‘I forever reside in the eight types of murtis and in the Sant.

Whenever a jiva attains a human body in Bharat-khand, God’s avatārs or God’s sādhus will certainly also be present on earth at that time. If that jiva can recognize them, then he becomes a devotee of God.
There is no greater status than that of a sādhu. In a kingdom, the queen’s authority is equal to that of the king. In the same way, that sādhu possesses as much majesty as God.

The powers of such a person are such that since it is God who sees through his eyes, he empowers the eyes of all of the beings in the brahmānd; ... Therefore, such a Sant is the sustainer of the world.
A Sant with such a conviction is so highly respected by Me that even I place the dust of his feet on My head... He is so great that his darshan alone can redeem countless wretched jivas.

Manifest are the words, manifest the vow divine; Manifest the devotee, manifest the Lord supreme There is not a single tale of redemption apart — For whatever one beholds here, is the Lord Himself in sight and heart.
The Satpurush is me, and I am that Satpurush Shriji Maharaj has personally said this Believe that the Satpurush is my own murti There is no difference between us.

Blessed, blessed is that wise and holy saint, In whom the self has turned within and merged — For such a saint is none other than God Himself... Nishkulanand declares with joy: In the company of such a saint, The sun of divine bliss rises within one’s heart.

Intense love for the Satpurush is the only means to realizing one’s ātmā; it is the only means to realizing the greatness of the Satpurush; and it is also the only means to having the direct realization of God.

If a person develops conviction in the guru - who is the manifest form of God - in the same way that he has conviction in the non-manifest deities, then, as a result, he attains all of the arthas which are described as attainable.
Valmiki praised the Lord of the forest, Vyasa sang of the Lord of the herds; By the power of His manifest devotion and glory, His divine fame spread vast and boundless

Today, there is no mantra more powerful than the Swaminarayan mantra. It makes even the poison of a black cobra ineffective and dispels the desire for material pleasures. With it, one becomes brahmarup and is freed from the bondage of kāl, karma and māyā. That is how powerful this mantra is. Therefore, always chant it.

Transcending that Brahma is Parabrahma, Purushottam Nārāyan, who is distinct from Brahma, and is the cause, the supporter and the inspirer of Brahma. With such understanding, one should develop oneness with one’s jivātmā and with that Brahma and worship Parabrahma while maintaining a master-servant relationship with Him.

An aspirant engages in discourses, sings bhajans and talks about God, but does not believe, “I am not this body.” Therefore, 24 hours-a-day remember, “I am not the body, but I am the ātmā, who lives in the body. I am brahman, akshar and within me Paramatma Parameshwar Purushottam himself is eternally present.”

We are born to accomplish two things. One, to become aksharrup – in this, the body is a hindrance; and two, to join with God – in this, company (of worldly people) is a hindrance in many ways. These two faults must be removed.

When worshiping God, one should not let fear of others who oppose worship of God enter their mind. ... Muktanand Swami says, God will save him from drowning. Metaphorically, drowning refers to drowning in the ocean of māyā.

A true devotee of God would never fall back in his devotion to God, even if he were to lose his body or wealth; just as a sati discards all possessiveness of this world to burn with her husband on the cremation pyre. ... Those who have such firm resoluteness are foremost. They never experience misery. Muktanand Swami says they are extremely happy.
In order to please God, I desire only to serve devotees of God in this life and all subsequent lives.
Only those who have accumulated a great number of merits from performing good deeds receive the opportunity to serve God’s Sant, but those who have a few merits do not.

When a person who wishes to worship God receives an opportunity to serve God and His devotees, he should serve them considering it to be his extremely great fortune. Moreover, he should do so only with bhakti for the sake of pleasing God and for his own liberation - not for the sake of receiving praise from others.
Remain as the servant of God. If you attain a low position, consider it your great fortune. Bhav (Shiva), Brahmā, and others certainly cannot find a place to sit near God.

By remembering God while performing activities, one remains at peace within. Seeing the peace within the devotee, the great Sadhu is pleased. And when the great Sadhu is pleased, one’s jiva becomes blissful.
My mind never becomes satiated with spiritual discourses, devotional songs, talks related to God or meditation of God. All of you should also do the same.

The means to transcend māyā is as follows: When the jiva comes into contact with the manifest form of Shri Purushottam Bhagwān - who is beyond māyā and who is the destroyer of māyā and all karmas - or the Sant who has attained that God, then by accepting their refuge, the jiva can transcend māyā.

Therefore, if one practices satsang with absolute sincerity, then no fault will remain in one’s heart, and one will become brahmarup in this very lifetime.

He whom we wish to attain after death, we have attained during this life; there is nothing more left to attain. If this truth is not understood properly, the jiva remains weak. First, Maharaj’s upāsanā; second, Maharaj’s commands; third, attachment with the great God-realized Sadhu; and fourth, friendship with the devotees. These four principles are the life-force of the jiva and they should never be given up.
Devotees should maintain oneness with each other. The more one devotee becomes one and united towards another, the dearer he becomes to Me.

All devotees who worship God are divine. One who understands, accepts, and reflects upon this important message becomes immersed in divine joy and conquers the world. He remains constantly blissful and his joy never wanes.
The Bhakta of God is indeed nothing but a form of Brahma. That is why one should never perceive human traits in him.

I consider this assembly of satsangis to be far greater than the assemblies in Shwetdwip, Golok, Vaikunth and Badrikāshram; and I see all of these devotees as being extremely luminous. Indeed, I swear by this assembly of sādhus that there is not even the slightest untruth in this matter. Why do I have to swear in this manner? Because not everyone understands such divinity, nor can they see it; that is why I have to swear.

In no way should one abandon one’s loyalty to God and His Bhakta, even if while keeping that loyalty one’s reputation increases or decreases, or one is honored or insulted, or one lives or dies. In addition, one should not allow an aversion to develop towards them.
Obeying God’s commands and upāsanā are the two wings. Never let go of them. Then, one can easily go to Akshardham. Of that there is no doubt.

He realizes, ‘The countless wonders which have occurred in the past, those which are currently taking place, and those which will occur in the future are all only due to the manifest form of God that I have attained.
At present we do not realize it, but we have attained God so we are fulfilled.

Since we have offered our body, mind and wealth to God, then now, only the will of God is our prārabdha; besides that, there is no other prārabdha for us. Therefore, regardless of whatever pain or pleasure we may encounter by the wish of God, we should not become disturbed in any way; we should be pleased with whatever pleases God.

If God seats us on an elephant, we should remain happy by sitting on an elephant; and if He seats us on a donkey, then we should remain happy by sitting on a donkey. Everything happens by the will of God. So, just as a dry leaf is blown in the air according to the direction of the wind, we should also remain dependent on Him and joyfully worship God, not allowing any frustration to enter our minds.

There are two means by which inner peace remains and no agitation arises: one is to worship God and the other is to understand God as the all-doer. Then, if we get happiness we should enjoy it and if we encounter misery we should tolerate it. It is said, “Dāsnā dushman Hari ke’di hoy nahi, jem karashe tem sukh ja thāshe.” – “God is not an enemy of the devotee, whatever he does will bring happiness.”
